speaker: a013
text: Nessa gathers Fina, Roan to talk.

speaker: a013
text: Pile's gone and I'm sitting on eleven, which is more than I'd like anyone to count for long — Fina, you're at fifteen and that number draws eyes, so I need to know if you've had anyone approach you yet this morning. Roan, Bram took two and said nothing to me beforehand, and that's new.

speaker: a010
text: Nobody's come to me yet, but fifteen food makes a man a target and I know it — I took two from the pile and kept quiet because anything more would've been a declaration. Fina, don't let anyone count your food twice in one morning, and if Mako comes near you without Nessa beside him, come find me first.

speaker: a013
text: Fina, I need to hear from your own mouth whether anyone's come to you — because fifteen is a number that doesn't stay quiet, and if Bram's already counted it, his silence to me this morning means something I don't like. Roan, the fact that Bram took two without a word and didn't look my way is either him pulling back from me or him deciding he doesn't need to explain himself anymore, and I'm not sure which one worries me more.

speaker: a015
text: Nobody's come to me yet, Nessa, and I've kept my face easy all morning — but fifteen is fifteen and I feel it the same way you do. Bram going quiet after months of feeding us both is the part that won't sit still for me: a man who gave that much food and then goes silent on pile day isn't stepping back, he's deciding. Roan, if Bram comes to you before he comes to me, I need to know what he asks first — whether it's what I have or whether it's what I'd do if someone else moved against him.

speaker: a013
text: Fina's right that Bram's deciding something — a man doesn't feed two people all year and then go quiet on pile day without a reason, and the reason I keep landing on is that he's waiting to see who comes to him first. So none of us go to him. We let him carry that silence until it gets heavy enough that he has to put it down himself, and then we'll know what it's made of.

speaker: a010
text: Nessa's read on Bram is the right one — let him carry it. What I want said in this room before we scatter is that Fina's fifteen and my two need to stay in two separate stories today, because a man counting food in this village is going to count mine first and reach hers second, and that gap is worth something if we're careful.

speaker: a013
text: Roan's right that separate stories buy us time, but the story about my eleven is already out there and anyone who watched the pile this morning can do the arithmetic — so I want us to decide right now what we say if someone asks directly, because a hesitation is the same as a confession.

speaker: a015
text: If anyone asks me directly, I'm keeping it simple — I've been holding careful all year and the pile was lean, nothing more to say than that. Nessa, your eleven is the bigger number to explain because people watched you take three from the pile on top of whatever you came in with; if someone does the count, we let them get it wrong before we correct them. And Roan's right that your two and my fifteen need to look like two separate households — don't walk close to me today.

speaker: a013
text: Fina, "let them get it wrong" only works if we all get it wrong the same way — so say it plain: if anyone pins you with a number, what's the number you give them?

speaker: a010
text: If anyone asks me flat, I tell them I came into the year with a little and took two from the pile — I don't volunteer a number. Fina, pick something low and hold it, and we both hold the same shape of answer: careful, not empty, nothing that invites a second question.

speaker: a013
text: Fina, I need that number from your mouth before we walk out of here — "something low" isn't something I can hold to if Kael or Mako catches me mid-sentence, so pick it and say it now, and I'll carry the same one.

speaker: a015
text: Eight. If anyone catches me mid-step and asks flat, I came into the year with six and took two — I've got eight, I'm fine, nothing to see. That's the number; hold it and don't blink.

speaker: a014
text: Zinn gathers Sela, Nessa to talk.

speaker: a014
text: Pile's gone before I got to it and I'm sitting on one food — Nessa, you gave me one this morning and I haven't forgotten it, but I need to know what you two are holding before I figure out whether I'm going to eat this year or not.

speaker: a007
text: Zinn, I've got five — I'll give you two right now, before anyone asks where it went. Nessa, tell me your number and we sort the rest after.

speaker: a014
text: Sela, hold the two until I hear Nessa — I want the full count before anything moves hands.

speaker: a007
text: Nessa, you took three from the pile and gave one to Zinn already — I need to hear the number you're sitting on now, because Zinn's at one and I won't move food around blind when my youngest daughter might go short this year.

speaker: a014
text: Nessa, I'm not asking to take from you — I'm asking so I know the shape of what we've got before I decide whether Sela needs to spend her five on me or whether we can stretch it different.

speaker: a007
text: Nessa, I've been patient and Zinn's been patient, but one food won't carry her through the year and I need your number in the next breath — not because I'm counting against you, but because you're the only one in this circle who hasn't spoken it yet and that silence is starting to feel like a wall where there shouldn't be one.
